_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never shipped to the student before a teacher/marker PDF is actually generated. English-only, never translated. See CLAUDE.md §5.

markingScheme.criterion: Accurately describes the pattern (CO₂ concentration rose steadily/continuously between 1960 and 2020, and the rise got steeper), quoting at least two of their own logged CO₂ year readings from the Investigation Record.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine logged readings that show the rise (for example about 317 ppm in 1960 and about 414 ppm in 2020); approximate values and wording are fine.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('it went up') with no actual readings quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains the cause: burning fossil fuels (coal, oil, natural gas) releases carbon that was stored underground for millions of years as CO₂, and the amount burned grew as the world's energy demand grew.
markingScheme.accept: Any scientifically equivalent phrasing: combustion, burning fuels, power stations, vehicles, industry adding CO₂ to the air. Mention of emissions rising over the decades earns the growth element.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'pollution' or 'humans' with no link to burning fossil fuels.

markingScheme.criterion: States clearly whether this evidence supports or contradicts the hypothesis made in the Hypothesis stage, and why.
markingScheme.insufficient: Restating the hypothesis without judging it against the evidence.

markingScheme.criterion: Compares coal and wind as PRIMARY energy sources: both are captured directly from nature before conversion; coal is non-renewable (finite, cannot be replenished) while wind is renewable (constantly replenished).
markingScheme.accept: Must correctly name both as primary and state the renewable/non-renewable difference; exact keywords not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only that wind is 'cleaner' with no classification.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains the mechanism: burning coal releases stored carbon as CO₂, whereas a wind turbine generates electricity from moving air without burning anything, so it adds no CO₂ while operating.
markingScheme.accept: Any equivalent wording about combustion releasing CO₂ versus no combustion in wind generation.

markingScheme.criterion: Concludes that the switch would reduce (slow) the CO₂ being added to the atmosphere, naming both options in the conclusion.
markingScheme.accept: Slowing the rate of increase is the expected answer; a strong answer may add that CO₂ already in the air stays, so concentration would keep rising more slowly rather than instantly falling.
markingScheme.insufficient: A vague statement ('it would be better for the environment') with no reference to CO₂ added to the atmosphere.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply), using each question's point-by-point markingScheme above (award each point independently unless it states a dependsOn, in which case only award it if the point it depends on was also awarded) and the rubric's level descriptors, which restate the same points as bands — do not invent extra criteria beyond what is defined here. Each rubric row's 'source' states exactly which question's marks it equals; never award a criterion's marks a second time on top of the question-level marks they restate. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy (6 marks). Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept' field; do not penalise spelling or grammar unless it actually interferes with meaning. Use the raw Investigation Record data (the 'CO2 year' rows) to verify any claim the student makes about their own readings. Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
